title: DoubleLiftChart y-axis padding breaks for all-negative data: padded yMax falls below the true maximum, pushing the zero line and bars above the chart top
description: yMax = allVals.reduce(max) * 1.1 and yMin = Math.min(0, reduce(min) * 1.1). The *1.1 'headroom' multiplier assumes the extremes are non-negative. When all decile values are negative (possible for regression targets / signed residual-style averages), multiplying a negative maximum by 1.1 makes yMax MORE negative than the actual largest value, so the data point lies above the plotted top of the axis. Worse, zeroY = yScale(0) is then computed for a 0 that sits above yMax: (0 - yMin)/ySpan > 1, so zeroY < marginTop, i.e. the zero baseline and every downward bar (drawn from zeroY for d.value < 0, lines 142/144) render above the chart's top edge / get clipped. Standard pricing diagnostics (frequency/severity averages) are non-negative so this is an unusual-input edge, but the code claims to support negatives (it has a yMin<0 zero-line branch at line 132 and signed-bar logic at 141-144), so the padding logic is internally inconsistent with that support.
evidence: data = [{actual:-1,...},{actual:-2,...}]: allVals=[-1,-2]; yMax = max(-1,-2)*1.1 = -1.1; yMin = min(0, min(-1,-2)*1.1) = min(0,-2.2) = -2.2; ySpan = 1.1. For the largest value actual=-1 (>=0 is false) -> actualY = zeroY = yScale(0) = marginTop + chartH - ((0 - (-2.2))/1.1)*chartH = marginTop + chartH - 2*chartH = marginTop - chartH < marginTop. Bar top is a full chartH above the chart. Correct padding for the negative side would multiply the negative extreme outward (e.g. min*1.1 only when min<0, and pad the positive extreme by *1.1 only when max>0).
